solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Nothing in bra, sadly? Turn around, I'll give you a tumble

definitions.note: a clause spoken by the performer, standing for the noun

indicators.note: something sadly done is done badly, so the letters are knocked out of their proper order
a word placed in another sits within it, so one piece goes inside
to go around something is to enclose it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage
the letter O looks like zero
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky come-on: an empty bra, a request to turn around, and a promise of a roll in the hay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like an instruction to spin round, but it is a stage turn, a performer's act; 'a tumble' is also slang for sex, the surface's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus acrobat performs tumbles and somersaults, so this performer is literally someone who will give you a tumble.

clue.text: "I shrunk as I ballsed up as a leader"

indicators.note: to balls something up is British slang for making a mess of it, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, all ten of them

explanation.surface: A mock confession from a politician who admits he diminished himself by bungling the top job.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was the UK Conservative Prime Minister from 2022 to 2024; the whole quotation is put in his mouth, which is the satire.
explanation.definitionFit: He served as British Prime Minister and Conservative Party head, so naming him as a national leader is an accurate factual description.

clue.text: see 27dn.
Two sorts of crack keenly sensed by one?

definitions.text: Two sorts of crack keenly sensed by one?

blocks.note: surface reading: splits or fissures, or perhaps wisecracks, detected by someone sharp
setter's reading: the drug crack cocaine picked up by an animal's keen nose at customs

explanation.walkthrough: Crack is both cocaine and a quip or fissure; 'keenly sensed' hints at a nose, and the animal trained for drug searches is the answer, with the whole clue as its description.
explanation.definitionFit: Police and customs use trained canines that detect narcotics like crack cocaine by smell at airports and borders.

clue.text: Toothy thing, decrepit type getting end away

indicators.note: sending the end away removes the final letter of the word

blocks.note: an old crock is a worn-out person or vehicle

explanation.surface: Something with big teeth, and an ageing wreck who is having a bit of sexual luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex, which is the surface joke; cryptically it just drops the last letter of CROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile, shortened to croc, has a long snout lined with conspicuous sharp teeth, so it is a toothy creature.

clue.text: Death to fickle sexy escort!

indicators.note: something fickle keeps changing, so the letters change their order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A furious cry wishing doom on an unfaithful, attractive companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Death to' reads as a curse; it is only the letters to be rearranged, and 'fickle' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive person one goes out with romantically is informally called a hot date, the one who accompanies you for the evening.

clue.text: Very difficult time of ultimately despotic dictator married to goddess

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only final letters are kept

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the final letter of the word
Isis is the Egyptian mother goddess

explanation.surface: A nation's dark hour under a tyrant who has wed a divinity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' applies to both following words, taking the last letter of each, not just of despotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a moment of acute danger or trouble, a turning point when things are at their hardest.

clue.text: Imagined situation of no raise being negotiated with Conservative leader intervening

indicators.note: terms under negotiation are being reworked, so the letters get rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter
to intervene is to come between, so one letter is inserted

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Pay talks in which a Tory chief steps in, and the hypothetical outcome is no pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven letters of 'no raise' are rearranged, and the single C from the Conservative sits second of all.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a hypothetical sequence of events, a possible situation pictured in advance rather than real.

clue.text: Steal Native American power

blocks.note: the Cree are a Native American people
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: An accusation that indigenous authority has been taken by theft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steal' reads as theft but here means move quietly, as in stealing out of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal into a room is to move stealthily and quietly, which is exactly what creeping means.

clue.text: Weapon possessed by Trump is to 'liberate'

indicators.note: what is possessed by a phrase is held inside its run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the ends and starts of these words

explanation.surface: A gun owned by Trump, who plans to use it to set people free, with ironic quotation marks.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the last letter of Trump through 'is to' into the first letter of liberate.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a small handgun, one kind of firearm among many weapons.

clue.text: Else, not Ernie?

blocks.note: first meaning: in other circumstances, or else
second meaning, read in two words: a different comedian sharing the surname

explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was half of Morecambe and Wise, a much-loved British comedy double act; a Wise who is not Ernie is some other Wise, split 5,4.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in different circumstances or or else, a direct synonym used in speech and writing.

clue.text: see 27dn.
Moralistic author wants a model to do a turn

indicators.note: turning round makes something face the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
to model is to pose for an artist or camera

explanation.surface: A preachy writer demands that a fashion model twirl for him.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the model's word turns round; the A stays put in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek fabulist's animal stories each end with a moral lesson, so he is the classic moralising writer.

clue.text: Shakespearean character joins Private Eye - that's rich!

blocks.note: Prospero is the magician in The Tempest
the clue appears in Private Eye, so the magazine is 'us'

explanation.surface: An actor from a Shakespeare play signs up at the satirical magazine, and someone scoffs at the irony.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is the British satirical magazine this crossword runs in, so it refers to itself as US.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosperous person is wealthy and successful, so the adjective is a straightforward synonym for having plenty of money.

clue.text: European Community in protest, surprisingly not to be made public

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it
a surprising result is an unexpected one, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: EC is the standard abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demonstration against the European body that, oddly, is kept under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: The EC sits inside the rearranged letters of protest, after the first four.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-secret information is classified at the highest level and must be kept confidential from everyone outside.

clue.text: Just an earl's OBE wangled

indicators.note: to wangle is to fiddle or manipulate, so the letters are manipulated into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Merely a nobleman's honour obtained through string-pulling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' pretends to mean merely; it is the definition in its sense of fair. An OBE is a British honour, the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A just decision is fair and sensible, which is what reasonable means when describing a judgment or demand.

clue.text: Large body needs bracing (not hip)

blocks.note: the United Nations, a large international body
bracing weather is fresh and cool

explanation.surface: A fat person requires a corset, apart from around the hips.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets pretend to exclude the hip from the bracing; they actually hold the definition, with hip meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip is slang for fashionable, so something not hip is unfashionable and lacks style, which is uncool.

clue.text: Rash doctor holds one on getting head

indicators.note: whatever holds something has it inside

blocks.note: MD is a Doctor of Medicine
a means one
a cap is the head or top of something, like a mushroom's

explanation.surface: A GP treats a patient's skin eruption, one that comes up on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like the skin complaint but is the adjective meaning reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: A madcap scheme or person is wildly impulsive and reckless, acting without thought, which is what rash describes.

clue.text: Character lies about getting oats and more besides

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tells tales about eating oats, and much more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is a written letter here, not a person in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a breakfast mix of rolled oats with dried fruit, nuts and seeds, so it is oats plus other ingredients.

clue.text: Accuse Trump, say, of having one medium orangey colour

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
peach is a soft orange-pink shade

explanation.surface: Charging the former president with, among other things, a moderately orange complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks Trump as an example: he was twice charged by the House of Representatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Impeachment is the formal charging of a public official such as a president with misconduct by a legislature.

clue.text: What you might do after waking up second time: prepare to be sick

definitions.text: What you might do after waking up

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
T is the abbreviation for time
to retch is to heave as if about to vomit

explanation.surface: A grim morning: waking up a second time and feeling ready to throw up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second time' reads as a repeat awakening but is two single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: On rising people often extend their arms and limbs to loosen stiff muscles, an everyday morning action.

clue.text: Millions standing by ex-President wanting money for ex-running mate

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for millions
Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower
pence are British coins

explanation.surface: Millions of supporters stand by a former president who is short of cash for his former vice-presidential partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The ex-President looks like Trump, but it is Eisenhower, known as Ike.
explanation.definitionFit: Pence was Trump's vice-presidential candidate in 2016 and 2020, his partner on the ticket and no longer so.

clue.text: Getting hot in enjoyable nooky place

definitions.note: a punning phrase for 'place like a nook'

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

blocks.note: something enjoyable is nice
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Things heating up in a pleasant spot for sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Nooky is British slang for sex; read as nook-y it means nook-like, a small recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a small recess in a wall, a shallow alcove very like a nook or cranny.

clue.text: It's good to be a presenter and break completely with a lover

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a TV presenter hosts the show

explanation.surface: A TV personality's advice: presenting is great, and so is dumping your partner outright.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghosting, cutting someone off without a word, is recent slang, so the definition may be new to older solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ghost someone is modern slang for ending a relationship by abruptly cutting off all contact without explanation.

clue.text: Fear going topless, revealing boob

indicators.note: losing the top of a word removes its first letter

blocks.note: terror is extreme fear

explanation.surface: Nerves about sunbathing topless, and a breast on show.
explanation.walkthrough: Boob is British slang for a blunder as well as a breast, which gives the surface its joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is an embarrassing blunder, a silly mistake, so the noun is an informal synonym for a mistake.

clue.text: Actor's interpretation of sound of wind?

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: to wind something up is to roll it

explanation.surface: An actor's impression of the noise a gust makes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like moving air, but it is the verb rhyming with find: coil or roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is the part an actor plays, the character as the performer interprets it on stage or screen.

clue.text: Mark's a big shot on speed

blocks.note: a celebrity, a famous person
rate means speed, as in rate of travel

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark is a famous figure who takes amphetamines.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a name and speed like the drug; Mark is the verb, as in mark an anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark an occasion is to observe it with festivities, which is what celebrating a birthday or anniversary means.

clue.text: (& 12ac./3dn.) Fake news purveyor unmasked?

blocks.note: surface reading: a spreader of disinformation
setter's reading: with the face uncovered, a literal take on a shameless fibber

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for a shameless fibber is read literally: a teller of lies whose face is bare because the mask has come off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying openly and shamelessly is called barefaced, and spreading fake news is telling untruths.

clue.text: No second university could rule out Trump's role in Capitol attack?

definitions.note: names a role, while the answer is the person playing it

indicators.note: saying no to the second of a pair removes that occurrence
out means disordered or not in place, so the letters rearrange

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for university
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a courtroom could dismiss what Trump did on January 6th.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase could rule has two Us; the second one goes, and the remaining eight letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who conspires secretly with others toward an unlawful end is a colluder, as alleged of Trump over the riot.

clue.text: What fun for dithering Labour leader to get in charge!

indicators.note: dithering is wavering and unsettled, so the letters will not stay in order
the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the word
i/c is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Mockery at the prospect of an indecisive Labour boss taking command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dithering Labour leader' pretends to describe Keir Starmer; the dithering belongs to the preceding word.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is a bout of playful, carefree merriment, so the noun means fun or a lively romp.
